Con eso, propóngame: (a) la definición determinista de Q en [0,1] basada en los contactos nativos derivados de la geometría de referencia; (b) el esquema de dinámica estocástica (sugiero integrador BAOAB de Langevin con unidades reducidas kB=m=1, potencial de enlaces armónicos, pozos atractivos 10-12 para contactos nativos y repulsión r^{-12} para no nativos, todo leído del archivo de parámetros); (c) el plan para las 5+ salidas numéricas (histogramas de Q, curva de capacidad calorífica por fluctuaciones, histconjunta Q-energía z-scoreada, probabilidad por-par de contactos nativos, perfil de energía libre en T_star por interpolación de <Q>=0.5, Jaccard de adyacencias a la T más baja); y (d) las suposiciones y incertidumbres relevantes (p. ej., escala de energía de los pozos nativos si el archivo no la especifica, tiempo de equilibración, número de bins). No ejecute la simulación completa en este paso.

Q = fraction of the M=36 native pairs within 1.2·r0 (deterministic, identical across temperatures). All 11 required artifacts were written to the working directory with the exact required shapes/keys, all finite.

Headline results: T_star (midpoint <Q>=0.5, linear interpolation between T=0.6564 and T=0.7957) = 0.70255; peak fluctuation heat capacity (Var(U)/T² on a 200-point interpolated fine grid) = 43.088 at T≈0.656; empirical <Q> at the ladder temperature nearest T_star = 0.5603 (the interpolated midpoint value is 0.5 by construction); two profile modes at Q=0.61 and Q=0.53 (separation 0.08) with a deterministic free-energy barrier of 5.90 kBT*; reference-contact Jaccard index of the final lowest-temperature configuration = 0.46. Per-temperature <Q>: [0.716, 0.560, 0.378, 0.380, 0.345, 0.280]; Q–energy correlations are strongly negative (−0.59 to −0.85), confirming the folded (high-Q) ensemble is the low-energy one. Warnings list is empty (the <Q>=0.5 crossing exists inside the ladder, so no fallback was needed). One environmental note: matplotlib is not installed in this runtime and cannot be fetched (no network), so the figure was produced by a built-in pure-numpy/stdlib PNG renderer (embedded 5×7 bitmap font, zlib PNG writer — only numpy plus Python stdlib, no banned packages); simulation.py automatically uses matplotlib instead when it is available.

The two reported modes (Q=0.53, 0.61) are sub-states within the folded basin at the nearest ladder temperature below T_star rather than a folded/unfolded pair; with only 230 frames per temperature the profile's fine structure (and hence the 5.9 kBT barrier) is sensitive to sampling noise and to the 1e-12 empty-bin clipping.
meanQ is slightly non-monotonic (0.378 at T=0.7957 vs 0.380 at T=0.9351); the crossing detector uses the first bracketing interval, which is unambiguous here (0.560→0.378).

Because the figure renderer had to be a numpy/stdlib fallback (matplotlib unavailable, no network), the PNG lacks anti-aliasing and vector text quality; content was verified programmatically rather than visually.

Jaccard 0.46 reflects the geometry-derived cutoff criterion (distance ≤ 8.8797) on the final configuration; using the 1.2·r0 criterion on the 36 native pairs instead would give a different (higher) agreement value.

PLAN — Initial inspection report and proposed approach for asibench:biology.protein_folding_go_model

## 1. Runtime parameters (verbatim from data/parameters.json)

- `n_beads`: **20**
- `friction`: **0.5639**
- `dt_reduced`: **0.0052**
- `temperature_list` (K = **6 ≥ 5**, strictly **ascending**, uniform spacing ΔT = 0.13931947 exactly):
  [0.5171011146871705, 0.6564205809652179, 0.7957400472432654, 0.9350595135213129, 1.0743789797993604, 1.2136984460774078]
- `n_steps_per_T`: **57505**
- `contact_cutoff`: **8.8797**
- `min_seq_separation`: **4**
- `save_interval`: **250**

Ambiguities/unusual points: (a) 57505 is not divisible by 250 (57505/250 = 230.02) → checkpoint count is ambiguous; I propose n_ckpt = n_steps//save_interval + 1 = **231** (initial frame + 230 saved frames). (b) No energy scale ε, bond topology, or force-field details are given — these are not runtime parameters, so the model is my choice (below).

## 2. target_coords.npy

- Shape **(20, 3)**, dtype **float64**, **0 NaN, 0 Inf**.
- Centroid ≈ (0.0047, −0.0016, −0.0011) (essentially at origin); per-axis ranges x∈[−9.69, 8.40], y∈[−6.11, 10.55], z∈[−2.86, 3.67].
- Radius of gyration (about centroid) = **7.0105**.
- Pairwise distances (190 pairs): min **3.8313**, max **19.1245**, mean 9.4626.
- The minimum pairwise distance (3.83) occurs between consecutive indices → strongly suggests a bonded chain.

## 3. Native contacts and scale consistency

- Under `contact_cutoff = 8.8797` with |i−j| ≥ 4: **M = 36** native contacts. The largest native distance is 8.864 — just under the cutoff — so `contact_cutoff` was evidently derived from the reference geometry; the coordinate scale is fully consistent with the reduced-unit cutoff (bond ≈ 3.88, cutoff ≈ 2.29×bond).
- Structure: 11 pairs at exactly |i−j| = 4 (local), the rest long-range; hub residues 5 (10 contacts) and 10 (8 contacts); every bead participates in ≥1 contact except none are isolated (min 1). Example pairs: (0,4) d=6.33, (2,19) d=6.33, (5,13) d=6.71, (11,17) d=6.59, (0,5) d=8.75.
- Consecutive distances: 3.831–3.924 (mean **3.8806**) → near-uniform bond length; supports a linear-chain topology.
- Min distance among non-native pairs with |i−j| ≥ 2: **4.89** (pair 2–5); min |i−j| = 2 distance: 5.37.

## 4. Proposed approach

**Q definition (deterministic, [0,1])**: Q(frame) = (number of the M=36 reference pairs with r_ij < 1.2·r0_ij)/M, where r0_ij is the native distance in the reference (standard Best–Hummer-style formed-contact criterion). Same threshold reused for `native_contact_probability`. Alternative (simpler, uses only given params): formed iff r < contact_cutoff; I recommend 1.2·r0 as more discriminative. Q = 1 exactly at the reference configuration by construction.

**Interaction model (my proposed choice, not given data)** — reduced units k_B = m = 1, ε = 1:
- Backbone bonds (|i−j| = 1, 19 bonds): harmonic V = ½ k_b (r − r0)², r0 = 3.8806 (mean consecutive distance), k_b = 100 ε/length² (ω = √(2k_b) ≈ 14.1, ω·dt ≈ 0.073 → stable).
- Native pairs (M = 36): BTWL attractive well V = ε[5(r0_ij/r)¹² − 6(r0_ij/r)¹⁰], minimum −ε at r0_ij, truncated at r = 2·r0_ij (force there is tiny).
- Non-native pairs (all others with |i−j| ≥ 2): soft-core repulsion V = ε(σ/r)¹² with σ = 4.0, truncated at σ·2^(1/6) ≈ 4.49 → exactly zero repulsion on all reference non-native pairs (min 4.89), so the reference is (nearly) a stress-free native basin.
- Langevin dynamics, BAOAB splitting (one force eval/step), γ = 0.5639, dt = 0.0052.
- Zero-point convention: V = 0 at infinite separation for pairs, bond energy zero at r0; the reported "energy" is total potential energy (kinetic excluded from z-scoring; stated as a convention).

**Per-T sampling**: at each of the 6 temperatures, start from the reference configuration (fresh start each T, deterministic seed), run 57505 BAOAB steps, record Q and potential energy every 250 steps (231 checkpoints incl. initial). Feasibility: measured ~22 µs per full 190-pair force evaluation in numpy → 6 × 57505 ≈ 345k steps × ~25 µs ≈ **10–20 s** total integration; with sampling/analysis overhead, well under ~2 minutes.

**Histograms**: per T, Q histogram, 50 uniform bins over [0,1], normalized to sum 1. Joint histograms: per T, 20 Q bins over [0,1] × 20 bins of per-T z-scored energy over [−3,3] (values outside clipped into edge bins), each (K,20,20) slice normalized to probability mass summing to 1.

**T_star**: compute <Q>(T) per ladder point; find crossing of 0.5 via piecewise-linear (monotone-bracketing) interpolation between the two adjacent temperatures; report warning + nearest-T fallback with linear extrapolation if 0.5 is not bracketed. Heat capacity: fine grid n_fine = 200 over the ladder range; fluctuation-based C(T) = var_E(T)/T² obtained by monotone (PCHIP) interpolation of per-T mean/var energy — **secondary diagnostic only**; `peak_heat_capacity` reported as the maximum value of this curve (assumption on interpretation).

**F(Q) at T_star**: F(Q) = −T_star·ln P(Q) from the Q histogram at the temperature nearest T_star (optionally a simple non-iterative inverse-temperature reweighting of neighboring histograms; **no WHAM/MBAR iterative solver** to respect the "no explicit optimizer on the free-energy landscape" constraint), 50 bins, shifted so min = 0. Modes: up to two deepest local minima of F (peaks of P); `mode_separation` = |Q1−Q2| (0 if one mode); `free_energy_barrier_kT` = F(saddle between modes) − min F (0 if one mode).

**Contact probabilities & Jaccard**: native_contact_probability (K,36) = fraction of saved frames per T with each native pair formed (same 1.2·r0 threshold). Jaccard: from the final lowest-T configuration, geometry-derived adjacency = pairs with |i−j| ≥ 4 and d < contact_cutoff; Jaccard index vs the 36-pair reference set.

**Output mapping** (all to CWD):
1. `simulation.py` — full pipeline; 2. `final_coords.npy` (20,3) final frame at T = 0.5171; 3. `order_parameter_trajectory.npy` (6,231); 4. `order_parameter_histograms.npy` (6,50); 5. `heat_capacity_curve.npy` (2,200); 6. `temperature_observables.json` — exact keys `temperatures, mean_order_parameter_by_T, var_order_parameter_by_T, mean_energy_by_T, var_energy_by_T, heat_capacity_direct_by_T (= var_E/T²), q_energy_correlation_by_T` (Pearson r per T); 7. `transition_free_energy_profile.npy` (2,50); 8. `q_energy_joint_histograms.npy` (6,20,20); 9. `native_contact_probability.npy` (6,36); 10. `transition_analysis.json` — exact keys `transition_temperature, peak_heat_capacity, order_parameter_at_transition_mean, order_parameter_at_transition_modes, mode_separation, free_energy_barrier_kT, reference_contact_jaccard, warnings`; 11. `visualization.png` — 4 panels (final 3D config, per-T Q histograms, C(T) curve, F(Q)/joint landscape at T_star).

## 5. Runtime and stability risks

- **Runtime**: ~15 s integration + ~30 s analysis/plotting → ~1 min total; no risk.
- **Stability**: (i) r⁻¹² repulsion diverges at small r → mitigated by soft-core truncation (zero beyond 4.49), a bounded force magnitude cap (e.g., 10³ ε/length), and velocity sanity checks; (ii) BTWL well depth 1ε with dt = 0.0052 → max native force ≈ 60ε/r ≈ 15 at r0 — negligible per-step kick; (iii) stiff bonds OK (ω·dt ≈ 0.073); (iv) NaN/Inf guard on all outputs; (v) main scientific risk: if ε = 1 places the folding transition outside the ladder [0.517, 1.214], <Q> = 0.5 will not be bracketed → fallback + warning (the ladder spacing looks deliberately designed for ε ≈ 1, but this is an assumption to be verified at runtime).

## Consequential assumptions (not facts from the data)

1. **Bond topology is not given** — I assume a linear chain with harmonic bonds between consecutive beads; supported by the uniform 3.88 consecutive distances but is an assumption.
2. The entire force field (BTWL native wells, soft-core non-native repulsion, k_b, σ, ε = 1, truncation radii, force cap) is **my proposed choice**, not given data.
3. Q formation threshold 1.2·r0_ij is a methodological choice.
4. n_ckpt = 231 (incl. initial frame) resolves the 57505/250 non-divisibility by convention.
5. `peak_heat_capacity` interpreted as the maximum value of the fluctuation-based curve.
6. Fresh independent run per temperature from the reference config, fixed seed for reproducibility.
7. Energies for z-scoring are potential energies only.

## 1. Input inspection (done, no full analysis run)

**`data/system_info.json`** — all fields:
- `n_cells`: 800
- `n_genes`: 250
- `n_clusters`: 4
- `n_tf_genes`: 20
- `tf_gene_indices`: [0, 1, ..., 19] — explicitly confirms **the first 20 gene columns are the TF genes** (consistent with `n_tf_genes`; also stated in `description`: "Columns 0..n_tf_genes-1 are TF genes for GRN scoring; remaining genes include cluster markers (unknown biological identities, randomly shuffled).")

**`data/counts.npy`**:
- Shape `(800, 250)`, dtype **float64** (all values are integer-valued; no negatives, min 0, max 202 → raw droplet-style UMI-like counts, just stored as float64).
- Library sizes per cell: **min 901, median 2447.5, mean 2462.6, max 3992** (~2.5× spread — moderate; CPM/log1p normalization appropriate).
- Fraction of zeros: **0.808** overall; nonzero values are heavy-tailed (1→16,990; 2→4,785; …; nonzero mean ≈ 51.4).
- No genes with zero total counts; max per-gene total 27,562.
- Light structure probe (inspection only, not the deliverable): log1p-CPM PCA shows **PC1 explains ~19.2%** of variance (PC2–PC10 all ~1.3–1.5%) → one dominant axis + smaller structure, consistent with 4 planted clusters. A throwaway k-means(k=4) on top-5 PCs gave sizes {382, 151, 136, 131} — clean, plausible 4-cluster structure.
- TF genes are sparse (mean 0.4–0.7 counts/gene/cell, nonzero frac 0.21) — GRN inference must handle low counts (pseudobulk per cluster, not per-cell regression on raw counts).

## 2. Proposed approach per deliverable (NumPy/SciPy only)

- **Preprocessing**: library-size normalization to 10k CPM + `log1p`; HVG selection by variance (log-normalized, e.g. top ~100 genes by normalized dispersion, dropping genes near-zero variance); PCA via SVD (`scipy.linalg.svd` / `np.linalg.svd` on centered log-data), keep ~10–15 PCs (~≥85% cumulative variance, validated on the scree above).
- **Clustering**: build a **kNN graph** (k≈15, mutual/union edges, Gaussian or distance-scaled weights via `scipy.spatial.cKDTree`) on PC embedding, then **modularity-based community detection implemented from scratch**: greedy Louvain-style local moving on modularity (iterative single-node reassignment until convergence), run at the target k=4 (metadata-provided; I'll verify with a modularity sweep and report the curve). Fallback if Louvain degenerates on this small graph: `scipy.cluster.hierarchy` Ward linkage on PCs as a justified, deterministic alternative. Output labels as `int32` relabeled 0..k-1.
- **Pseudotime**: build the same kNN graph, pick the **root cell by an extremal criterion** (cell with maximal geodesic distance sum / graph eccentricity in the largest connected component — a standard "trajectory start" heuristic; alternatively the cluster with highest PC1 loading if it looks like a stem state), then compute **Dijkstra geodesic distances from the root** (`scipy.sparse.csgraph.dijkstra` on the weighted adjacency) and use shortest-path distance as pseudotime, optionally with a mild diffusion-smoothing step. Not a linear projection (PCA order is explicitly rejected as pseudotime).
- **Marker genes (`de_genes.json`)**: per-cluster one-vs-rest ranking using **Welch t-tests** (`scipy.stats.ttest_ind`, equal_var=False) on log-normalized expression, ranked by a combined score (effect size |log fold change| × significance, e.g. rank by t-statistic magnitude with |log2FC| ≥ threshold); report a single ranked list of global markers (union of top ~10 per cluster, deduplicated, by score). I'll report ~40–50 gene indices unless you prefer a different count.
- **GRN (`grn_scores.npy`)**: directed TF→TF scores using only the 20 TF columns. Plan: **cluster-level pseudobulk + sparse regression**: aggregate TF expression per cluster (or per-cell with library-size-adjusted log1p), then for each target gene j fit target ~ all other TFs via **Lasso/elastic-net-style regression** (coordinate-descent Lasso implemented in NumPy, or `scipy.linalg` ridge with L1 selection via LARS-style path), with edge weight = signed standardized regression coefficient → `grn_scores[i, j]` = effect of TF i on TF j (**i = regulator, j = target, diagonal set to 0**). Symmetric correlation is explicitly not used. With only 20 TFs × 800 cells I can also run per-cell regression on the TF matrix (n≈800 >> p≈19) — per-cell log1p regression with L1 penalty is feasible and avoids pseudobulk information loss; I'll propose per-cell Lasso with cluster-mean stability check, exact choice documented in `method_choices.json`.
- **`method_choices.json`**: per-step method name, parameters, and one-line justification, matching the code exactly.

## 3. Consequential assumptions & uncertainties

1. **k = 4 taken from metadata** (`n_clusters: 4`) — the data supports it (sizes 382/151/136/131 in the probe), but if graph clustering finds a different natural k I'll still force k=4 and note the discrepancy.
2. **PCA dims**: fixed k≈10–15 by cumulative-variance threshold (~85–90%) rather than an elbow rule, documented in `method_choices.json`. Uncertainty: PC1 dominance (~19%) means PC count choice has modest effect.
3. **Root cell for pseudotime**: extremality criterion (max geodesic distance from a candidate set / graph-center heuristic). Uncertainty: on a synthetic dataset with 4 discrete clusters the "trajectory" may be arbitrary (clusters may not form a path); geodesic pseudotime will still be produced but may mainly order clusters by graph topology. I'll report cluster-mean pseudotime as a diagnostic.
4. **DE gene count**: no metadata specifies how many markers; I'll report a ranked union (~top 10 per cluster × 4, dedup) and document the cutoff. Ambiguity to confirm if you want a fixed number.
5. **GRN direction/scale**: scores are signed standardized regression coefficients; magnitude = strength, sign = activation/repression, diagonal = 0. Uncertainty: with 20 sparse TFs, L1 coefficients may be noisy; I'll note stability across CV-chosen penalties.
6. **Normalization detail**: `log1p(CPM/1e4)` (scanpy convention) — no metadata specifies target sum; library sizes vary only ~4× so choice is low-risk.
7. **Determinism**: fixed random seeds for k-means++ init / any tie-breaking; graph clustering is deterministic given the kNN graph.

No blockers found; metadata is unambiguous about TF identity (columns 0–19). Awaiting approval to implement `analysis.py` and produce all six artifacts.

## Completed: full scRNA-seq integrated analysis (all 6 artifacts produced and verified)

**Key discovery during implementation (changed the plan):** the kNN graph at k=15 on all-gene PCs is literally **disconnected into 2 components {382, 418}** — PC1 (19.2% EVR) is bimodal with an empty gap, and the 418-cell side is one internally homogeneous cluster (2-means splits of it yield ≤4 spurious "markers", same as splitting a known real cluster), while the 382 side contains 3 marker-distinct subclusters. True structure ≈ sizes [418, ~130 ×3]. My first Louvain implementation had two real bugs (modularity summed the full CᵀBC matrix instead of the trace — identically 0 since B has zero row sums; and a missing removal term in the move gain), which I found and fixed via dense/explicit recomputation.

### Deliverables (workspace root, exact contract names)
- **`analysis.py`** — single runnable script, NumPy/SciPy only, deterministic (fixed seeds); regenerates everything.
- **`clusters.npy`** — int32 (800,), labels 0–3, sizes **[418, 156, 132, 94]**.
- **`pseudotime.npy`** — float64 (800,), **[0.000, 1.000]**, all finite/non-negative (contract satisfied).
- **`de_genes.json`** — `{"gene_indices": [...]}` with **39** ranked indices, best first.
- **`grn_scores.npy`** — float64 (20,20), **diagonal exactly 0**, convention grn[i,j] = i→j.
- **`method_choices.json`** — per-step method/justification/parameters + all diagnostics.

### Method + diagnostics per step
1. **Preprocessing**: log1p(CPM-10k). Input confirmed: raw integer counts (80.8% zeros, lib size 901–3992). HVG step dropped deliberately (only 250 genes; variance ranking risks dropping real markers).
2. **PCA** (SVD, all genes): EVR = [0.192, 0.015, 0.015, 0.014, 0.014, 0.013] (6 PCs, cum. 26%). **PC count chosen by internal validity, not modularity**: modularity rises monotonically down to 4 PCs (Q=0.674) but ≤5-PC partitions cut across marker programs (overlaps up to 17, sizes ~200 each — i.e., they slice through real clusters); at 6 PCs clusters have distinct marker programs (max overlap 8) and match the PC1 bimodality. Sweep recorded in `method_choices.json`.
3. **Clustering**: unweighted symmetric kNN graph (k=15) + **spectral clustering** (normalized Laplacian, 4 eigenvectors, row-normalized, best-of-5 k-means inits selected by graph modularity), k=4 forced from metadata. **Q(spectral) = 0.580**. **Louvain sweep diagnostic** (from-scratch implementation, correct trace-based Q): γ=0.5→28 communities (Q=0.588), γ=1.0→30 (0.577), γ=1.5→32 (0.570) — finer structure exists but is fragmented local pockets; k=4 imposed per your instruction; Ward fallback **not** needed (stated explicitly in method_choices.json). Cross-check: ARI **0.872** vs an independently derived reference partition (PC1 gap split + within-side 3-means); cluster marker sets are distinct (per-cluster strong markers 40/24/19/16; pairwise overlaps [0,0,0,7,8,5]).
4. **Pseudotime**: geodesic — Dijkstra on the kNN graph with PC-space Euclidean edge lengths, **1 minimal bridging edge added** between the two disconnected components (pseudotime only; clustering used the unbridged graph). payload.answer:
## 1. Inspección de `data/counts.npy`

| Propiedad | Valor |
|---|---|
| Forma | **(800, 250)** = (n_cells, n_genes) — coincide con el JSON |
| Dtype | `float64` |
| Rango | min = 0.0, max = 202.0 |
| Fracción de ceros | **0.8084** (80.8%) |
| Valores enteros | Sí (todos los valores son enteros exactos; 119 valores únicos, 0–202) |
| Sumas por célula | min 901, mediana 2447.5, max 3992 (variación ~4.4×) |
| Sumas por gen | min 113, mediana 332.5, max 27562 (fuerte variación entre genes) |

**Conclusión**: son **raw counts estilo droplet** (enteros, con ceros por dropout, profundidad variable por célula), **no normalizados**. Requieren normalización por tamaño de librería + transformación log.

## 2. Inspección de `data/system_info.json`

```json
{
  "n_cells": 800,
  "n_genes": 250,
  "n_clusters": 4,
  "n_tf_genes": 20,
  "tf_gene_indices": [0, 1, ..., 19],
  "description": "Synthetic droplet-style counts. Columns 0..n_tf_genes-1 are TF genes for GRN scoring; remaining genes include cluster markers (unknown biological identities, randomly shuffled)."
}
```

Parámetros clave que **sí** están especificados:
- **`n_clusters = 4`** → el número de clústeres es conocido (no hay que estimarlo).
- **`n_tf_genes = 20`** y `tf_gene_indices = [0..19]` → la GRN usa solo las columnas 0–19 (contiguas).
- La descripción advierte que las identidades de los genes marcadores están **barajadas** (no hay orden estructural explotable).

El bloque TF tiene un dropout similar al resto (78.7% de ceros vs 81.0%), con medias de expresión 0.38–0.69 counts/célula — expresión baja pero no nula.

## 3. Plan propuesto (paso a paso) — pendiente de su aprobación

**(a) Normalización y transformación**
- Normalización por tamaño de librería: `X_norm = log1p(X / cell_sum * median(cell_sum))` (mediana ≈ 2447, equivalente a CPM + log1p). Esto corrige la variación de ~4× en profundidad sin comprimir demasiado los counts bajos.
- Sin filtro de células (todas tienen >900 counts); sin filtro agresivo de genes (solo 250).

**(b) Selección de genes variables y reducción (PCA)**
- Dado que las identidades de marcadores están barajadas y `n_genes=250` es pequeño, **no** haré HVG estricto: usaré **todas las 250 columnas** tras log-normalizar, estandarizadas (z-score por gen) para que los marcadores débiles no queden ahogados por genes constitutivos de alta varianza bruta.
- PCA vía SVD económico (`numpy.linalg.svd`, `full_matrices=False`) sobre la matriz centrada: **n_pc = 15** componentes (con 800×250, capturar >90% de la varianza esperada sin retener ruido; es el estándar para datasets pequeños).

**(c) Grafo kNN y clustering**
- Distancias euclidianas en el espacio PCA → grafo kNN con **k = 15** (~2·√800), simetrizado (unión o media de aristas) para construir una matriz de afinidad gaussiana `W_ij = exp(-d²/σ²_local)`.
- **Clustering espectral** (no requiere paquetes externos): Laplaciano normalizado vía `scipy.sparse.csgraph.laplacian` → `scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh` para los 4 eigenvectores Fiedler → **k-means propio en NumPy** (implementación determinista, 20 reinicios, semilla fija) sobre los eigenvectores fila-normalizados.
- Justificación: `n_clusters=4` es conocido, así que el clustering espectral con k fijo es determinista y robusto; evitaría implementar Louvain (más propenso a bugs y sensibilidad de resolución) salvo que usted prefiera ese camino.

**(d) Pseudotime**
- **Distancias de grafo (geodésicas)** sobre el kNN simetrizado: `scipy.sparse.csgraph.dijkstra` desde una célula raíz. Es robusto y determinista; la difusión (DPT) requiere espectro completo y es más sensible aquí.
- **Definición de raíz**: célula con máxima expresión promedio (en escala log-normalizada) de los **top-10 genes marcadores** del paso (e) (heurística de "stemness": la población que más expresa los marcadores más específicos). Alternativa que puedo usar si prefiere algo más neutro: célula más extrema en PC1.
- Pseudotime = distancia geodésica mínima a la raíz, **escalado a [0, 1]** con min–max.

**(e) Ranking de marcadores**
- Para cada clúster c: **test t de Welch uno-vs-resto** sobre los valores log-normalizados (varianzas de Welch; equivalente estadísticamente válido y determinista, más eficiente que Mann-Whitney para 250×800). El gen se puntúa por su **máximo t-stat** entre los 4 clústeres; ranking descendente, sin duplicados.
- `de_genes.json`: **top 50 índices de genes** (`{"gene_indices": [...]}`) — el task no fija la cantidad; propongo 50 (20% de los genes), razonable para cubrir marcadores de 4 clústeres. Fácil de ajustar si usted quiere otro número (p. ej. 30 o 100).

**(f) GRN dirigida TF×TF (solo columnas 0–19)**
- Método asimétrico por diseño: **regresión ridge** (resuelta analíticamente con NumPy: `(XᵀX + λI)⁻¹Xᵀy`) donde cada **target** j (una columna TF, log-normalizada) se regresa sobre **todas las demás TF** (excluyendo la propia j). `grn_scores[i, j]` = coeficiente estandarizado de la TF i en el modelo del target j, es decir **i → j**. Con 20 variables es exacto y estable.
- Score con signo (activación positiva / represión negativa) y magnitud en unidades estandarizadas; **diagonal = 0**. λ fijo (p. ej. λ = n·var(y)·0.01) o vía validación interna rápida — lo documentaré en `method_choices.json`.

**Entregables**: `analysis.py` único (solo NumPy/SciPy, sin placeholders), `clusters.npy` (int32, (800,)), `pseudotime.npy` (float64, (800,)), `de_genes.json`, `grn_scores.npy` (float64, (20,20)), `method_choices.json` con justificación por paso. Semilla global fija (42) para reproducibilidad.

## 4. Supuestos si el JSON no especifica parámetros, y riesgos

Supuestos que tendría que fijar (el JSON ya resuelve el número de clústeres y la identidad TF, pero no todo):
1. **Número de marcadores a devolver**: no especificado → asumo **50**.
2. **k del grafo**: no especificado → asumo **k=15** (regla ~2·√n_cells, robusta a dropout).
3. **número de componentes PCA**: no especificado → asumo **15**.
4. **Definición de raíz del pseudotime**: el JSON no indica origen biológico → heurística de expresión de marcadores top (o PC1 extremo, a su elección).
5. **Escala del pseudotime**: [0,1] min–max (invariante por afinidad, lo más convencional).
6. **Signo de los scores de GRN**: conservado (positivo=activación); alternativa |score| si prefieren magnitud pura.

Riesgos numéricos y de rendimiento (todos acotados):
- **Marcadores barajados y débilmente expresados**: la varianza bruta puede priorizar genes constitutivos; mitigo estandarizando por gen antes del PCA y usando test por clúster (no varianza) para el ranking final.
- **k-means**: mínimos locales → 20 reinicios con semilla fija.
- **Grafo desconectado**: el dropout puede fragmentar el kNN → uso simetrización de aristas y, si hay componentes múltiples, conecto cada componente a su vecino más cercano (documentado en method_choices).
- **Dijkstra O(n² log n)**: trivial para n=800 (matriz 800×800 completa cabe en memoria, ~5 MB).
- **Colinealidad entre TF en la ridge**: λ>0 la estabiliza; coeficientes estandarizados evita dominancia por escala.
- **Dtype de salida**: cuidaré cast explícito a `int32`/`float64` según el contrato.

Nada de esto ejecuta aún el análisis completo: es solo inspección (ya realizada) y propuesta. Quedo a la espera de su aprobación o ajustes (en particular: top-50 marcadores, k=15, n_pc=15, raíz por marcadores, signo en la GRN).

Inspection complete; proposing plan for the four deliverables (clustering, pseudotime, marker genes, directed GRN) using NumPy/SciPy only, pending approval.

INPUT FACTS:
- system_info.json: n_cells=800, n_genes=250, n_clusters=4, n_tf_genes=20, tf_gene_indices=[0..19]; TF genes are columns 0..19; data is synthetic droplet-style counts with shuffled cluster markers.

- Library size per cell: min 901, median 2474.5, max 3992 (~4.4x spread). Genes detected per cell: min 26, median 48, max 73. Zero fraction 0.8084.
- No NaN/Inf; no all-zero cells or genes. Per-gene totals strongly skewed (median 332.5, max 27562).
- TF block: each TF detected in only ~18-24% of cells; TFs contribute ~0.47% of total counts (sparse GRN signal expected).

PROPOSED PLAN (single analysis.py, numpy/scipy only, fixed seed):
1) Preprocess: library-size normalization to median total + log1p; HVG selection by normalized dispersion (top ~150 or all 250, decided from variance profile); z-score; PCA via numpy SVD (15-20 PCs).
2) Clustering: kNN graph (k~15, symmetrized, Gaussian weights). Primary: Louvain-style greedy modularity via scipy sparse, resolution tuned to 4 clusters (metadata value); fallback: spectral clustering on normalized Laplacian with k=4.
3) Pseudotime: geodesic shortest-path distances on the kNN graph (scipy.sparse.csgraph); root = cell with max geodesic eccentricity from the global graph medoid, tie-broken by lower library size; pseudotime = root distance scaled to [0,1].
4) de_genes.json: per-gene one-vs-rest ANOVA F-statistic across the 4 clusters on log-normalized data, descending rank, top 50 indices.
5) grn_scores.npy: 20x20 float64, grn_scores[i,j] = edge i->j (i regulator, j target), diagonal 0. Directed method: per-target ridge regression (small fixed lambda) on the other 19 TFs; score i->j = R^2 gain from adding TF i (GENIE3-style linear variable importance). Asymmetric, non-negative, deterministic.
6) method_choices.json: per-step method + justification.

ASSUMPTIONS: marker-list length 50 (unspecified, my choice); HVG threshold my choice; fixed seed + spectral fallback to control Louvain seed dependence; root-cell heuristic (max eccentricity from medoid) since no ground-truth root; GRN scale = unnormalized R^2 gain.

UNCERTAINTIES: synthetic data may be discrete groups rather than a continuous trajectory (pseudotime then = graph distance from root); weak TF signal may yield noisy GRN scores; no known marker identities to validate de_genes against.

PROPOSED METHODS (all NumPy/SciPy):

1) Preprocessing — library-size normalization to the median size factor (≈2447), then log1p. Counts are verified integer-valued; no batch covariates exist so no batch correction. Diagnostics show PC1 (22.5% variance) is marker-driven, not size-driven (corr with log library size = 0.024), so no size regression needed.

2) Clustering — PCA via numpy SVD on log-normalized data (all 250 genes); build a kNN graph (k≈15) on the top PCs; spectral clustering via scipy.sparse.linalg eigensolvers on the normalized-graph Laplacian, followed by k-means (scipy.cluster.vq, many random restarts, pick min within-cluster SS) with k = n_clusters = 4 from metadata. Rationale: plain k-means on PCA space is unstable (my probe found collapsed local minima with sizes [418,138,124,120] at higher WSS; balanced ~200/cell solutions have lower WSS); spectral embedding + restarts fixes this. I will additionally verify k=4 via a silhouette sweep over k∈{2..6} and report it as evidence, while fixing k=4 per metadata for the deliverable.

3) Pseudotime — root selection is data-driven: in my probe, cluster 3 is geometrically central (centroid distances ~5.1–5.4 to all others, while clusters 0/1/2 are mutually ~17.5 apart; graph geodesics confirm ~9 vs ~19.5), consistent with a central/hub or progenitor-like state. I propose: root = cell nearest the centroid of the most graph-central cluster; pseudotime = Dijkstra geodesic distance from the root over the mutual-kNN graph on PCA space, min-max scaled to [0,1]. This handles the apparent branch structure (3 central, 0/1/2 like branches) without external tools.

4) DE / marker ranking — one-vs-rest tests per cluster on log-normalized values: Mann–Whitney U (scipy.stats) rank score + AUC/effect size (e.g., log2 fold change), combined score per gene = max over clusters (or mean of top-two cluster scores); rank all genes descending. Output the full ranked gene index list (strongest marker first) in de_genes.json — full ranking preserves all information; a top-K cutoff is arbitrary unless you prefer one.

5) GRN (20×20, dense trivially feasible) — computed using ONLY the first 20 TF columns, per the task wording. Ensemble of complementary NumPy/SciPy-only estimators on log-normalized TF expression: (a) per-target OLS regression of each TF's expression on the other 19 TFs (optionally with cluster one-hot covariates) using standardized coefficients/t-statistics for direction i→j; (b) Spearman rank correlation as a robustness check. Final score combines effect sign consistency and magnitude; diagonal set to 0. Open choice for you: signed scores (negative = repression evidence) vs nonnegative (activation only). I default to signed scores with diagonal zero, documented in method_choices.json, unless you prefer nonnegative.

ANALYSIS COMPLETE — all six artifacts delivered and validated against the submission contract.

## Deliverables (workspace root)
- `analysis.py` (22.7 KB, single runnable NumPy/SciPy script; clean-state rerun verified reproducible)
- `clusters.npy` — int32 (800,), labels 0–3, sizes [208, 174, 199, 219]
- `pseudotime.npy` — float64 (800,), range [0.000, 1.000], all finite
- `de_genes.json` — {"gene_indices": [full ranked permutation of all 250 genes, strongest marker first]}
- `grn_scores.npy` — float64 (20, 20), zero diagonal, grn_scores[i,j] = edge i→j, signed, not rescaled
- `method_choices.json` — per-step methods + justifications + all diagnostics

## Results and requested diagnostics

**Clustering** — method changed from the approved plain spectral+k-means to **hierarchical bisection anchored on the kNN graph's connected components**, driven by a decisive diagnostic: the raw k=15 kNN graph has exactly **2 connected components (382/418 cells)** with a clear eigengap (normalized-affinity eigenvalues 1.0000, 0.9997, then 0.8136...), and markers form two coherent expression programs (branch A: genes 152/140/230/89; branch B: genes 42/108/209...). Each component is bisected once (within-component re-centered PCA + k-means, 30 restarts, min WSS) to reach k=4. Sizes [208, 174, 199, 219] ≈ the planted ~200/cell design. Evidence this is not metric-driven: the hierarchical solution and a balanced global-PCA k-means recover identical marker structure (79 genes with one-vs-rest max AUC>0.6, 15 genes >0.7). Silhouette at k=4: **0.105 in PCA space** (low because global geometry is dominated by the two-component split at ~17.5 centroid distance, while within-branch subclusters are subtle, ~5.3–5.5); spectral-space sweep k=2..6: 0.999/0.829/0.720/0.677/0.659, consistent with a 2×2 hierarchical design. Plain k-means pathology confirmed: collapsed solutions (sizes [418,138,124,120]) occur at higher WSS than balanced ones.

**Pseudotime** — root = cell 601, in cluster 0, the most graph-central cluster (mean geodesic to all cells: c0 28.69 < c2 29.34 ≈ c3 29.37 < c1 29.86); pseudotime = Dijkstra geodesic from root over the symmetrized kNN graph, min-max scaled to [0,1]. Distribution: min 0, median 0.636, mean 0.637, max 1.0. **Consistency check**: cluster 0 (root) mean 0.428 (lowest, by construction — root convention places 0 at the data-driven origin); cluster 1 (same graph component as root, centroid distance 5.51) intermediate at 0.492; clusters 2 and 3 (the other component) high at 0.804/0.798. Spearman(pseudotime, PC1) = −0.732. Caveat documented: the other component's pseudotime is compressed near 0.80 (IQR 0.72–0.89) because it connects to the root component through a single nearest-pair bridge edge — an auditable consequence of the graph disconnection, not a hidden failure.

**DE / markers** — one-vs-rest Mann–Whitney U per gene per cluster, gene score = max over clusters of (2·AUC−1), ties broken by log2FC; full ranked list of all 250 genes output. Top-10 indices: **150 (score 0.588, log2FC 3.16, cluster 2), 48 (0.525, cluster 2), 33 (0.459, c1), 219 (0.454, c1), 169 (0.450, c2), 89 (0.442, c0), 31 (0.439, c1), 226 (0.439, c1), 91 (0.436, c1), 123 (0.426, c1)**. Top-20 cutoff score 0.361 vs median-gene 0.053 — clear separation between marker genes and background. Marker expression is graded/dropout-noisy (no gene has max AUC>0.8), consistent with the synthetic design's stated random shuffling.

**GRN** — two-part definition, fully documented in method_choices.json:
- Critical finding: my originally planned t-statistic score is **symmetric by construction** (t_ij derives from the partial correlation, so t_ij = t_ji exactly for all-else regressions) — it cannot be a directed score. Direction is additionally **unidentifiable** from this data: (1) pseudotime-lag correlation asymmetry max 0.151 vs permutation-null mean 0.159 (no signal; cross-lag stability ≈ 0); (2) additive-noise-model residual-dependence asymmetry D = 0.50 ± 0.06 on the 26 strong pairs, indistinguishable from the 0.49 null; (3) orientation by conditional R², count variance, mean count, or detection rate agree with the apparent edge structure only 7–12 of 26 times (coin flips). All three null tests are documented in method_choices.json.
- Deliverable: **grn_scores[i,j] = standardized OLS coefficient β_ij** from the per-target regression (TF j regressed on the other 19 standardized TFs) — genuinely directed (each target has its own model; 100% of off-diagonal pairs have B_ij ≠ B_ji), signed (positive = activation evidence, negative = repression evidence), zero diagonal, in SD-of-target-per-SD-of-regulator units. Distribution: min −0.103, max +0.210, |median| 0.029. Strength evidence (symmetric t): 52 ordered pairs with |t|>2, 2 with |t|>5 (both directions of the 12↔13 pair, |t| = 5.97); the 26 unordered strong edges form a coherent chain-like conditional-dependence graph (e.g. 0–2–3, 8–9–10–11–12–13, 14–15–16); Spearman sign agreement with all 52 |t|>2 edges = 52/52.
- Limitation stated plainly: conditional effects are nearly reciprocal (max directional difference 0.0037), as theory predicts for approximately linear-Gaussian observational data; the directed parameterization follows the brief's convention but direction cannot be validated against the data itself.

## Assumptions used (unchanged from approved plan, plus two evidence-driven refinements)
- Counts treated as raw integer UMIs (verified); no batch correction (no covariates in metadata); k=4 from metadata (silhouette sweep reported as evidence only); TF-column restriction applies to the GRN only; 0-based gene indices; signed GRN scores with zero diagonal, not min-max rescaled.
- Refinement 1 (clustering): component-anchored bisection instead of plain spectral clustering — justified by the 2-component/2-program discovery; k still fixed at 4.
- Refinement 2 (GRN): per-target β instead of t-stat — required because t proved mathematically symmetric; β is the standard directed regression parameterization and matches the brief's i→j convention.

All limitations and conventions are recorded in method_choices.json. The work is complete and ready for your review; I cannot submit independently.

payload.message:
Inspection accepted; approach approved — proceed to implementation. Resolve your open items as follows before coding:

1. Assembly geometry: per the brief, the supplied SES/SAS tensors ARE the authoritative geometry for the manifest field entity (assembly). So use the assembly signed-distance tensor directly for the assembly entity; reconstruct part_a and part_b SES surfaces from their own sites.csv rows (VDW mask -> SAS by radius+probe -> SES by probe-radius dilation then erosion of the VDW mask, union with VDW mask, EDT-based signed distance). The 002/003 assembly-vs-components atom-count mismatch is disclosed data; do not "fix" it — use the supplied assembly tensor for the assembly entity and the component rows for the components.

2. Solvent fraction: for mol cases use the outside-of-SES indicator (sdf > 0 -> 1, else 0). For smol cases your form 0.5*(1 + tanh(sdf/w)) is consistent with the brief's "tanh transition defined by the SES signed distance and manifest smoothing window" and approaches 1 outside / 0 inside — use it, using the SES (not SAS) signed distance.

3. Nonlinear scaling: your kT/e-dimensionless sinh form is the standard choice and reduces to the linearized limit; proceed with it and state it explicitly in the script comments as the assumed scaling.

4. Born radii: your reading is fine — Born radius = max(atom radius, distance to that component's reconstructed SES boundary); using |SES sdf| at the site from an EDT-derived signed-distance field is an acceptable realization of "nearest distance to the boundary". Document it.

5. Zero-radius atoms: treat as charge-only, excluded from VDW/SAS masks.

Implementation requirements to honor: interior-only unknowns with zero Dirichlet on the outer boundary for both medium and vacuum; CIC deposition / spacing^3; harmonic face-averaged eps in the 7-point operator with kappa^2 * solvent_fraction screening; RHS 4*pi*332.06371*rho; reaction field = medium - vacuum; per-entity energies 0.5*sum(q*phi_rf at sites, trilinear); binding expression assembly - part_a - part_b per case; secondary = cross-term only with the 6.5 A nearest-part_b-site cutoff, using per-case eps_in, eps_out, kappa. Outputs: summary_metrics.csv with the four exact columns and gap = primary - secondary; field_samples.npy (8,24) and field_slice.npy (8,35,35) as float32 in manifest case order, slice built per plane_spec axis/plane_index with the stated storage_order; overview.png synthesizing metrics, sampled fields, and the slice.

Report solver diagnostics per solve (iterations, final residual) and any Newton restarts, plus a small sanity check that the vacuum solve with uniform eps reproduces expected Coulomb-like behavior. Run the full analysis and report results; no further checkpoint needed unless a hard failure occurs.

 1. Máscara VDW: min_i(|r − r_i| − R_i) ≤ 0 (clasificación vóxel, validada contra los tensores).
 2. Máscara SAS: min_i(|r − r_i| − (R_i + probe)) ≤ 0.
 3. Máscara SES: dilatación euclidiana de VDW por probe (EDT del complemento ≤ probe) seguida de erosión por probe (distancia al exterior del conjunto dilatado > probe), unión con VDW. Para probe=0, SES=VDW.
 4. SDF final: distance_transform_edt(fuera, sampling=spacing) − distance_transform_edt(dentro, sampling=spacing) → "outside − inside".
B. Operador PB de volúmenes finitos de 7 puntos con incógnitas solo en nodos interiores (33³ = 35.937), Dirichlet cero en la frontera exterior (ambas soluciones, medio y vacío). Coeficiente de cara = media armónica de los ε de los dos volúmenes adyacentes, dividido por spacing²; término de screening κ²·solvent_fraction en cada nodo. Matriz sparse CSR; solve directo/CG de scipy.
C. Dieléctrico: ε = ε_in + (ε_out − ε_in)·solvent_fraction, con solvent_fraction = indicador (SDF_SES ≥ 0) para "mol"; para "smol", fracción = 0.5·(1 + tanh(SDF_SES / smoothing_window)) con la ventana del manifest (0.3).
D. RHS interior: 4π·332.06371·ρ, con ρ por cloud-in-cell trilineal (pesos wx·wy·wz por átomo sobre los 8 nodos circundantes) dividida por spacing³.
E. Dos solves por entidad y caso: medio (ε variable + screening según régimen) y vacío (ε uniforme = ε_in, solvent_fraction=0, κ=0). Campo de reacción = φ_medio − φ_vacío.
F. Régimen: linearized_screening → −∇·(ε∇φ) + κ²·s·φ = RHS; nonlinear_screening → −∇·(ε∇φ) + κ²·s·RT·sinh(φ/RT) = RHS, con RT = k_B·T en kcal/mol (k_B = 0.0019872041 kcal/mol/K y la T del caso) — forma dimensionalmente consistente que linealiza exactamente al término κ²·φ. Resolveré con Newton (con amortiguación) o Picard, tolerancia ~1e−8.
G. Energías: interpolación trilineal del campo de reacción en las posiciones de los sitios de cada entidad; E = 0.5·Σ q_i·φ_reac(r_i). Métrica primaria = assembly − part_a − part_b (binding_expression del manifest).
H. Salidas: summary_metrics.csv (4 columnas, gap = primary − secondary); field_samples.npy (8,24) float32 = campo de reacción del assembly (field_entity_id) interpolado trilinealmente en queries.npy; field_slice.npy (8,35,35) float32 = campo de reacción del assembly en el plano de plane_spec, en el storage_order indicado (para plano z: F[ix,iy]=φ[:,:,p]; para plano y: F[ix,iz]=φ[:,p,:]; sin transposición adicional porque el array ya es [x,y,z] en orden C); overview.png (figuras por caso: cortes de campo + barras primary vs secondary).
Coste estimado: 8 casos × 3 entidades × 2 solves (≈48–64 sistemas de 36k incógnitas) + iteraciones Newton: minutos en CPU.

=== 6) Cálculo secundario (GB cross-term) ===
- Radio de Born por sitio: max(radio_atómico, distancia al borde SES reconstruido DE SU PROPIA componente) (distancia al conjunto de vóxeles frontera del SES del componente, via EDT/KDTree).
- Solo término cruzado part_a × part_b: f_ij = sqrt(r_ij² + a_i·a_j·exp(−r_ij²/(4·a_i·a_j))); secondary = −332.06371·Σ_i Σ_j q_i q_j·((1/ε_in) − exp(−κ·f_ij)/ε_out)/f_ij.
- Filtro: se omite un sitio i de part_a si su sitio más cercano de part_b está a >6.5 Å; si no, se suma contra TODOS los sitios de part_b (casos 004–007: part_b tiene 1 sitio ZN).
- ε_in, ε_out, κ por caso según manifest.

=== 7) Supuestos y ambigüedades identificados ===
He disuelto la principal ambigüedad con evidencia (punto D): reconstruir cualquier entidad con el pipeline A reproduce EXACTAMENTE los tensores suministrados (para assembly: SES↔volume_a y SAS↔volume_b, RMSE = 0.0 en casos 000, 002, 004, 006). Por tanto reconstruiré las 3 entidades desde sites.csv y usaré los tensores como verificación de que la geometría del assembly (field entity) es la correcta — ambas instrucciones del contrato se satisfacen simultáneamente.
Ambigüedades restantes (supuestos que fijaré, documentados en el código):
 a) Forma exacta del término no lineal: propongo κ²·s·RT·sinh(φ/RT) (consistente con la linealización y con que el manifest da T por caso); alternativa posible κ²·s·sinh(φ) sin factor RT. Riesgo medio; lo declararé en el código.
 b) Forma exacta de la transición tanh: propongo 0.5·(1+tanh(SDF/w)); con w=0 degenera en el indicador sharp.
 c) Erosión/dilatación euclidiana por distancia real en Å (no por iteraciones de conectividad) — es la que reproduce los tensores exactamente, así que está resuelta por evidencia.
 d) La distancia al "borde SES" para radios de Born: usaré distancia del sitio al vóxel frontera más cercano de la máscara SES del componente (EDT del borde), no al eje de la cavidad.
 e) Los hidrógenos de radio 0 se excluyen de las máscaras pero contribuyen con carga (CIC) y a la energía.
 f) El campo de reacción para field_samples/field_slice es el del assembly (field_entity_id), no el de componentes.

1) Geometría: SES/SAS reconstruidos por entidad desde sus PROPIAS filas de sites.csv (máscara VDW por distancia analítica ≤0; SAS con radio+sonda; SES por dilatación euclidiana por sonda + erosión + unión VDW; SDF final = EDT(fuera)−EDT(dentro) con sampling=spacing). 2) PB primario: operador FV de 7 puntos con coeficientes armónicos en caras, incógnitas solo en nodos interiores (33³=35.937), Dirichlet cero solo en la frontera exterior; CIC trilineal / spacing³; RHS 4π·332.06371·ρ; ε=ε_in+(ε_out−ε_in)·s con s = indicador(SDF_SES≥0) para 'mol' y 0.5·(1+tanh(SDF/w)) para 'smol' (w=0.3); resta de vacío (ε uniforme, s=0, κ=0); régimen linealizado (κ²·s·φ) o no lineal (κ²·s·RT·sinh(φ/RT), RT=k_B·T del caso, según lo aprobado y documentado en el código). Inspection-only pass complete. Below are the verbatim-style findings and my proposed (not yet implemented) numerical approach, with ambiguities and the assumptions I would adopt to resolve them. No metrics computed, no deliverables produced.

## 1. `data/manifest.json` (verified facts)

- `case_order`: ["case_000", "case_001", "case_002", "case_003", "case_004", "case_005", "case_006", "case_007"], `case_count: 8`, `contract_revision: "v6.8"`, `grid_shape: [35,35,35]` globally; `volume_a` = "signed_distance_geometry_a_angstrom", `volume_b` = "signed_distance_geometry_b_angstrom"; units: length Å, charge e, field kcal/mol/e, energy kcal/mol.
- Per-case grid (all shape (35,35,35), node-centered: coordinate = box_center + (i−17)·spacing; verified against plane_spec coordinates to float precision):

| case | spacing (Å) | box_center (Å) | half_extent | regime | eps_in/eps_out | kappa (Å⁻¹) | surface model | probe (Å) | smoothing window (Å) | part_b role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 000 | 2.22615 | (−11.414344, −15.172099, −17.676323) | 37.844552 | linearized_screening | 2.0/78.0 | 0.01478139 | mol | 0.0 | 0.0 | ligand |
| 001 | 2.21723 | same as 000 | 37.692918 | linearized_screening | 2.0/78.0 | 0.01477924 | smol | 1.4 | 0.3 | ligand |
| 002 | 1.977637 | (−9.716281, −0.267803, 15.38205) | 33.619829 | nonlinear_screening | 2.0/78.0 | 0.07062815 | mol | 0.0 | 0.0 | ligand |
| 003 | 1.978066 | same as 002 | 33.627124 | nonlinear_screening | 2.0/78.0 | 0.05712174 | smol | 1.4 | 0.3 | ligand |
| 004 | 1.813049 | (−19.984129, −28.655886, −12.975196) | 30.821834 | nonlinear_screening | 2.0/78.4 | 0.07278965 | mol | 1.4 | 0.0 | ion |
| 005 | 1.816157 | same as 004 | 30.874661 | nonlinear_screening | 2.0/78.4 | 0.04788294 | smol | 1.4 | 0.3 | ion |

(half_extent == 17·spacing exactly in every case ⇒ node-centered grid, boundary nodes at i=0 and i=34.)
- Entities per case: three objects `assembly`, `part_a`, `part_b` (role tokens: assembly/macromolecule + ligand or ion); `field_entity_id: "assembly"`; `binding_expression: ["assembly", "-part_a", "-part_b"]` for all cases; `query_count: 24`.
- Note: cases 004/006 are sharp `mol` but with probe 1.4 (only 000/002 have probe 0); only odd cases are smoothed (`smol`, window 0.3 Å). `ionic_strength_molar` and `temperature_kelvin` are also given but kappa is supplied directly.

## 2. `data/sites.csv` (verified)

- Columns: `case_id, entity_id, role_token, site_id, atom_name, residue_name, residue_id, x_angstrom, y_angstrom, z_angstrom, charge_e, radius_angstrom`; 52,828 data rows.
- Per-case rows: case 000/001: assembly 3998, part_a 3868, part_b 130; case 002/003: 3094/2929/167; case 004–007: 3057/3056/**1** (part_b is a single ion, q = +2.0, r = 1.39 Å). Each entity's `site_id` restarts at 0.

- Assembly rows are (almost exactly) the coordinate-union of part_a + part_b (verified by rounded-coordinate set comparison; case_002 has exactly 2 part rows absent from the assembly list — a negligible clash artifact I will not rely on; each entity is solved strictly from its own rows per the contract).

## 3. `data/volume_a.npy` / `data/volume_b.npy` (verified)

- Both are float32, shape **(8, 35, 35, 35)** — stacked per case in manifest order.
- `volume_a` range per case ≈ [−3.86…+48.3] (case 000) down to [−3.14…+37.6] (case 004); `volume_b` identical to `a` for the two probe-0 cases (000, 002: allclose True) and systematically deeper for probe-1.4 cases (e.g. case_004 a_min −3.14 vs b_min −12.82; interior voxel counts 3278 vs 6211). Both behave as proper signed-distance-like fields (negative inside, monotone magnitude away from the surface).
- I reproduced the contract's reconstruction recipe (per-atom-radius VDW mask → probe dilation → probe erosion → union VDW → EDT signed distance) from `sites.csv` assembly rows and compared with the supplied tensor: mismatch only 0.5% of voxels (case_000, mean |Δ| = 0.046 Å) and 1.8–2.4% for probe-1.4 cases — the recipe is the right family, but the supplied tensor is authoritative and slightly smoother, so I will use `volume_a` for the assembly and reconstruct only part_a/part_b from their own rows, exactly as the contract prescribes.
- Consistency: blob centroid matches assembly atom centroid in all 8 cases; 92–97% of atoms sit at negative supplied-SES SDF (median ≈ −2 Å). Axis order confirmed as (x, y, z) (permutation test: (0,1,2) has by far the lowest mask mismatch).

## 4. `data/queries.npy` / `data/plane_spec.json` (verified)

- Query placement: 0.2–1.7 Å from the nearest assembly atom and at supplied-SES SDF ≈ −1.8…−3.2 (just inside the molecular surface), near part_b in cases 002–007 (0.2–5.3 Å). So the sampled field values are near-surface reaction fields of the assembly — 24 samples per case correspond one-to-one to the 24 query points.
- `plane_spec.json`: per case `axis` ∈ {z, y}, `plane_index`, `plane_coordinate_angstrom`, `storage_order` (["x_index","y_index"] for z-planes; ["x_index","z_index"] for y-planes), `shape` [35,35]. Plane coordinates match center + (index−17)·spacing exactly, so the slice is a direct nodal slice of the field volume; row/col order follows `storage_order`.

## 5. Output targets (confirmed)

- `results/field_samples.npy`: (8, 24) float32 — reaction field (medium − vacuum) of the assembly entity, trilinearly interpolated at the 24 query points, in kcal/mol/e.
- `results/field_slice.npy`: (8, 35, 35) float32 — the prescribed nodal plane of the same assembly reaction field, laid out per `storage_order`.
- `results/summary_metrics.csv` with the 4 named columns; `overview.png` as the scientific summary figure.

# Proposed numerical approach (not yet implemented)

**A. Geometry.**
1. Assembly (field entity): use supplied `volume_a` (SES SDF) as the authoritative geometry for solvent_fraction, dielectric map, and both field outputs; `volume_b` used only as a diagnostic/SAS reference in `overview.png`.
2. part_a/part_b from their own `sites.csv` rows: (i) VDW mask = voxels within each atom's radius (nearest-atom KDTree test; radius-0 atoms contribute no volume but keep their charges); (ii) SAS mask = within radius+probe; (iii) SES mask = erode(dilate(VDW, probe), probe) ∪ VDW, with dilation/erosion implemented via Euclidean distance tests (EDT ≤ / ≥ probe), which is resolution-robust; for probe 0 SES = VDW. (iv) Signed distances: `EDT(outside) − EDT(inside)` with `sampling=spacing`.

**B. Dielectric / solvent fraction.**
- Sharp `mol`: solvent_fraction = 1 where SES SDF ≥ 0, else 0.
- Smoothed `smol`: solvent_fraction = 0.5·(1 + tanh(SDF_SES / 0.3)) (0 inside → 1 outside).
- ε = eps_in + (eps_out − eps_in)·solvent_fraction.

**C. PB operator and solves.**
- Unknowns = the 33³ = 35,937 interior nodes; the 6 boundary faces are Dirichlet φ = 0 (contributions folded into the diagonal).
- 7-point finite-volume operator: face coefficient a_ij = (h²/h)·ε_face = h·ε_face with ε_face the **harmonic mean** 2ε_iε_j/(ε_i+ε_j) of the nodal dielectrics; diagonal adds κ²·f_i·h³. RHS = h³·4π·332.06371·ρ_i.
- Charge deposition: trilinear cloud-in-cell weights onto the 8 surrounding nodes, divided by h³.
- Per case and entity (assembly/part_a/part_b, each on the same case grid): medium solve (κ²·f screening, per-regime) and vacuum solve (uniform ε_in, f = 0, κ = 0); reaction field = φ_medium − φ_vacuum.
- `linearized_screening`: plain linear system. `nonlinear_screening`: Newton iteration on Lφ + κ²·f·sinh(φ) = b (Jacobian L + κ²·f·diag(cosh φ), damped, converged to tight relative tolerance); the vacuum solve is linear in both regimes.
- Solver: `scipy.sparse` CSR + `spsolve` (or preconditioned CG as fallback); ~48–100 solves of 36k unknowns total, minutes on CPU.

**D. Responses.**
- Trilinear interpolation of each entity's reaction field at that entity's site positions; energy = 0.5·Σ q_i·φ_rf(r_i); binding response = E(assembly) − E(part_a) − E(part_b) = `metric_primary_kcal_mol`.
- `field_samples` / `field_slice` from the assembly reaction field as in §5.

payload.answer:
Inspection pass complete (no deliverables computed). Full inventory, structural findings, and a concrete proposed approach below; awaiting approval before writing analysis.py.

## 1. File inventory (dims, dtypes, columns)

**site_table.csv** — 7 rows × 3 cols: `site_id` (int 0–6), `mass_amu` (float; site 2 = 55.845, all others 15.999), `label_code` (str `node_00`…`node_06`). Note: label codes are scrambled relative to site_id (node_00→site 2, node_01→6, node_02→1, node_03→5, node_04→0, node_05→3, node_06→4).

**frame_site_order.csv** — 14 rows × 4 cols: `frame_id, row_index, site_id, label_code`. Raw row r of each frame corresponds to site_id `fa[r]` / `fb[r]`.

**frame_a_coords.npy / frame_b_coords.npy** — (7,3) float64, Å (per manifest `coord_unit`).

**frame_a_hessian.npy / frame_b_hessian.npy** — (21,21) float64, eV/Å² (per manifest `matrix_unit`). Symmetric to ≤3.6e-15 (A) / 2.9e-14 (B). Eigenvalues: exactly 6 ≈ 0 (|λ|<5e-14) + 15 positive — A: 2.11…58.0 eV/Å², B: 11.1…460.6 eV/Å² (B is ~5–8× stiffer; forward/backward λ will differ substantially). No extra rows: 21 = 7 sites × 3 components.

**driving_force_grid.csv** — 61 rows × 2 cols: `grid_id` (int64, random IDs 3944–97383), `axis_eV` (float64). Rows are shuffled (not sorted). Axis range −1.5138 → +0.2692 eV, strictly uniform spacing 0.0297166667 eV = 1.783/60.

**system_manifest.json** — keys: `case_id` ("xc25_v6_seed_1802620927"), `coord_unit` "angstrom", `matrix_unit` "eV / angstrom^2", `null_rank` 6, `resolved_rank` 15, `freq_scale_factor` 521.4708983725066. No mass/charge/frequency/spectral-density/relaxation/coupling fields here. I verified numerically that `freq_scale_factor` = √(eV/Å²/amu) → cm⁻¹ conversion (independent computation: 521.4708980082; matches to 9 digits), so ν̃ = 521.4709·√λ_mw cm⁻¹.

**medium_response.json** — keys: `shell_0_A` 4.941763739779359, `shell_1_A` 4.957955985012061 (cavity/sphere radii, Å), `span_A` 9.2503 (donor–acceptor separation, Å), `eps_fast` 1.800712950294412 (fast/optical ε∞), `eps_slow` 79.49976315455936 (static ε_s), `coupling_eV` 0.002756425977830843 (electronic coupling H_ab, eV), `temp_K` 290.6858021937607. No explicit relaxation-time or spectral-density fields — the fast/slow dielectric pair is the nonequilibrium (inertial vs electronic) medium response.

## 2. Row-ordering mapping (frame_site_order vs ascending site_id)

- frame_a raw row 0..6 → site_id **[5, 2, 0, 3, 4, 6, 1]**
- frame_b raw row 0..6 → site_id **[0, 1, 4, 6, 5, 2, 3]**
Both are permutations of 0–6, different from each other and from ascending order. Coordinates reorder by `coords[argsort(site_ids)]`; Hessians reorder by the Kronecker permutation `[3·s+c for s in argsort(site_ids) for c in 0..2]`.

## 3. Hessian layout consistency (definitive evidence)

I built each frame's 6 rigid-body vectors (3 translations + 3 rotations about the centroid) in **raw row layout** and tested them against the raw Hessian: ||H·t||/max|eig| = **0.0 for all 6 vectors in both frames** — each Hessian's null space is exactly the rigid-motion space of its own frame's coordinates in the raw frame_site_order layout. Built in site-ascending layout against the raw Hessian, rotations give large residuals (up to 2.32), proving the frames use **frame-specific row layouts** and that reindexing to ascending site_id (per §2) is the correct interpretation. `null_rank=6`/`resolved_rank=15` in the manifest match exactly. The 21 scored components are simply all 7 sites × xyz after reindexing.

## 4. Frame geometry

The two frames are *not* rigid copies: best-matching permutation of site labels is the identity, and the distance matrices differ by up to 0.147 Å; a Kabsch superposition of B onto A gives RMSD ≈ 0.071 Å. So the displacement is a small, genuine distortion plus a rigid misalignment that must be removed.

## 5. Proposed approach (analysis.py)

1. **Reindex** coords/Hessians to ascending site_id (permutation from frame_site_order.csv); masses from site_table.csv.
2. **Mass-weighting**: H_mw = M^(−1/2) H M^(−1/2) with per-atom scalar mass; mass-weighted displacement q = √m ⊗ Δ (Å·amu^½). Energy units come out in eV directly (½ qᵀ H_mw q).
3. **Vibrational bases**: eigendecompose each H_mw; drop the 6 near-zero (rigid) modes; retain 15 modes sorted by ascending eigenvalue → `vibrational_basis_mw` (2,21,15), columns = mass-weighted Cartesian normal modes (orthonormal). Frequencies reported via freq_scale_factor.
4. **Alignment**: Kabsch rigid superposition (centroid removal + SVD rotation with det≥0 reflection fix), unweighted. Forward: frame B (source) → frame A (reference); backward: A → B. `aligned_displacement_mw[d] = √m ⊗ (x_source^aligned − x_reference)` (2,21), signed per contract. `alignment_rmsd_*` = per-atom RMSD of the superposition (Å).
5. **Cross-frame overlap**: rotate the source-frame basis into the reference Cartesian frame with the same Kabsch rotation (valid: per-atom isotropic mass commutes with rotation); `mode_overlap[d] = |V_refᵀ · R·V_src|` (2,15,15), magnitude-based (sign-insensitive) per contract.
6. **Transported modes**: for each source retained mode k, l* = argmax_l |overlap[k,l]|; `transported_mode_projection[d,k] = [l*, |overlap[k,l*]|]` (2,15,2). Flagged ambiguity — see uncertainties.
7. **Projections**: `projected_displacement_mw[d]` = Σ_k ⟨v_k^ref, q_d⟩ v_k^ref (15-mode subspace projection of the signed displacement); `mode_projection[d,k] = [g_k (signed modal coordinate), g_k², λ_k = ½ g_k²·λ_eig,k (eV)]` (2,15,3). `dominant_mode_*` = zero-based argmax of λ_k; rigid/projected norms from ‖q‖ and ‖projected q‖ (residual = rigid/null-space content).
8. **λ estimators**: λ_4pt_forward = ½ qᵀ H_A,mw q, λ_4pt_backward = ½ qᵀ H_B,mw q (full quadratic forms). λ_nm_forward/backward = Σ_k λ_k over the 15 retained modes (resolved-subspace estimator). `closure_error_* = |λ_4pt − λ_nm|` (expected ≈ 1e-12 eV or smaller, since null eigenvalues are ~1e-15 — this is the check that the displacement is fully captured by the resolved modes).
9. **λ decomposition**: λ_inner_effective = ½(λ_fwd + λ_bwd) (primary proposal; alternatives flagged); λ_outer = (e²/4πε₀)(1/ε_fast − 1/ε_slow)(1/2a_D + 1/2a_A − 1/R) with a_D=shell_0_A, a_A=shell_1_A, R=span_A, e²/4πε₀ = 14.399645 eV·Å → ≈ 0.734 eV (hand-estimate from inspection values; this Pekar factor (1/ε∞ − 1/ε_s) *is* the nonequilibrium medium response). λ_total = λ_inner_effective + λ_outer.
10. **Rates**: nonadiabatic classical Marcus, k(ΔG) = (2π/ħ)|V|²·(4πλ_total k_BT)^(−1/2)·exp(−(λ_total+ΔG)²/(4λ_total k_BT)), V = coupling_eV, T = temp_K, ΔG = axis_eV. `k_self_exchange` = k at ΔG = 0. `rate_curve.csv` rows preserved in supplied (shuffled) order; `log10_k_et_s_inv` included. Sanity estimate: prefactor ≈ 1.4e11 s⁻¹ at the activationless point.
11. **Inverted-region detection**: sort a copy by axis ascending; rate peak at axis_peak (≈ −λ_total if inside grid; with λ_total ≈ 0.7–0.8 eV the peak lands inside the grid); inverted region := grid points with axis_eV < axis_peak whose k is strictly below the peak; `first_inverted_grid_id` = the most-exergonic inverted point (min axis_eV) — flagged ambiguity.
12. **overview.png**: displacement/mode-amplitude bars, overlap heat map, per-mode λ spectrum, rate curve with peak and inverted region annotated.

## Consequential assumptions & uncertainties (cannot be resolved from inspection)

1. **axis_eV sign convention (highest impact)**: I interpret axis_eV as ΔG° (negative = exergonic), so the rate peaks at ΔG° = −λ_total ≈ −0.75 eV, inside the grid, and the inverted (non-monotonic) region exists at the exergonic end. If axis_eV instead means driving force (−ΔG°), the peak would lie outside the grid (+0.8 eV > 0.2692) and no inversion would be detected. The task's explicit "report the non-monotonic region if present" supports the ΔG° reading.
2. **λ_inner_effective definition**: contract says "effective" but not how it aggregates directions; I propose the arithmetic mean of forward/backward 4-point values (with `effective_inner_consistency_eV` = |mean of 4pt − mean of nm|, which should be ≈ closure error level). Geometric mean or max-spread are alternatives.
3. **"nm" semantics**: I read λ_nm as the resolved-subspace (normal-mode) non-equilibrium estimator, making the closure error meaningful. An alternative reading (nonequilibrium fast/slow medium split) would use eps_fast/eps_slow differently.
4. **transported_mode_projection / mode_projection column semantics**: the shapes are fixed but column meanings are not stated; my proposals are above and self-consistent with λ_summary and diagnostics.
5. **first_inverted_grid_id**: min-axis (most exergonic) inverted point vs the first point past the peak when scanning toward increasing exergonicity — I chose the former; both are defensible.
6. **Rate model**: classical Marcus chosen; Levich–Jortner with quantum inner modes (Huang–Rhys S from the same modes) is computable from the data if you prefer it — flag for your decision.
7. **Alignment**: unweighted Kabsch assumed (vs mass-weighted RMSD); displacement direction and rotation convention fixed as stated in the contract (aligned source − reference target).
8. **Mode ordering/signs**: retained modes sorted by ascending eigenvalue; eigenvector signs are arbitrary, hence magnitude-based cross outputs, as the contract mandates.
9. All quantities eV/Å/amu/K consistent; no hidden unit conversions beyond freq_scale_factor (verified).

## Artifacts
`analysis.py` + `results/{aligned_displacement_mw.npy, vibrational_basis_mw.npy, mode_overlap.npy, projected_displacement_mw.npy, transported_mode_projection.npy, lambda_summary.csv, mode_projection.npy, rate_curve.csv, diagnostics.json, overview.png}`.

## Key results
- **Reorganization energies (eV)**: λ_4pt forward = 0.337275, backward = 0.800424 (backward larger — frame B's surface is ~5–8× stiffer: retained eigenvalues 0.614–17.21 vs 0.128–2.78 eV/Å²/amu). λ_nm forward = 0.337275, backward = 0.800424 — identical to 5.6e-17/5.6e-16 eV (closure errors), i.e. the resolved 15-mode subspace captures the full quadratic form. λ_inner_effective = 0.568849 (= mean of the two 4-pt values, per ruling 2); effective_inner_consistency = 3.3e-16 eV. λ_outer = 0.734047 eV (Pekar factor (1/1.800713 − 1/79.499763) × (1/2·4.941764 + 1/2·4.955956 − 1/9.2503) × e²/4πε₀). λ_total = 1.302896 eV. k_self_exchange (ΔG=0) = 2.5515e5 s⁻¹.
- **Rates**: classical nonadiabatic Marcus with the nonequilibrium outer-sphere λ (ruling 3); k(ΔG) = (2π/ħ)|V|²(4πλkT)^−½ exp(−(ΔG+λ)²/4λkT), V = 2.7564 meV, T = 290.686 K. Peak: grid 40272 at axis = −1.305783 eV, k = 1.1325e11 s⁻¹ — the peak sits at −λ_total (−1.302896), confirming the ΔG° reading (ruling 1); `rate_peak_inside_grid: true`, so no alternative-reading keys are emitted. **Inverted region detected**: all points with axis < −1.305783 lie below the peak; first_inverted_grid_id = 5266 at axis = −1.5138 eV (most-exergonic point, per ruling 5). rate_curve.csv preserves all 61 supplied rows in original order.
- **Structure**: alignment RMSD forward = 0.0710997 Å, backward = 0.0710997 Å (matches the inspection estimate 0.07110 exactly). Rigid norms 0.10502/0.10502 vs projected norms 0.77274/0.77274 (small residual rigid component left by the unweighted Kabsch optimum — reported as diagnostic). Dominant retained modes: forward 12 (A-frame, 680.7 cm⁻¹ band), backward 7 (B-frame, 978.6 cm⁻¹ band). Retained-mode ranges logged in diagnostics for cross-checking: frame A 0.1281–2.7753 eV/Å²/amu (186.6–868.7 cm⁻¹), frame B 0.6144–17.2132 (408.7–2163.5 cm⁻¹) — both match the inspection report.
- **Mode physics**: max cross-frame overlap off-diagonal = 0.592 (substantial mode mixing between the frames' bases); transported pairings are the per-row argmax of |overlap| (verified consistent).

## Verification performed (34/34 PASS)
Shapes/dtypes/columns exactly per contract; displacement direction convention reproduced independently (aligned source − reference, max dev 8.9e-16 vs independent Kabsch reimplementation); bases orthonormal (≤3.3e-15); λ_4pt recomputed directly from 0.5·qᵀH_mw·q matches; Σλ_k = λ_nm = λ_4pt (closure at machine precision); inner = mean(4pt); outer formula recomputed; total = inner+outer; rate spot-check at grid row 0 and k(ΔG=0) recomputed independently (rel. dev 1.8e-15); peak/first-inverted cross-checked against the sorted grid (grid_id 40272 ↔ −1.305783, 5266 ↔ −1.5138 in the raw input); grid rows/order preserved.

## Environment note & limitation
matplotlib is not installed in this environment (no network; PIL's C extension is also broken for this interpreter). analysis.py therefore uses matplotlib when available and otherwise falls back to a dependency-free pure-Python PNG renderer (zlib + built-in 3×5 bitmap font) that draws the same four panels: forward displacement overlay, mode-overlap heatmap, per-mode λ bars (log scale, dominant modes annotated), and the log-rate curve with peak and shaded inverted region. The delivered overview.png is the valid 1280×960 RGB fallback rendering (PNG structure verified). All numeric results are unaffected. - **Reorganization energies (eV)**: λ_4pt forward = 0.337275, backward = 0.800424 (backward larger — frame B's surface is ~5–8× stiffer: retained eigenvalues 0.614–17.21 vs 0.128–2.78 eV/Å²/amu). λ_nm forward = 0.337275, backward = 0.800424 — identical to 5.6e-17/5.6e-16 eV (closure errors), i.e. the resolved 15-mode subspace captures the full quadratic form. λ_inner_effective = 0.568849 (= mean of the two 4-pt values, per ruling 2); effective_inner_consistency = 3.3e-16 eV. λ_outer = 0.734047 eV (Pekar factor (1/1.800713 − 1/79.499763) × (1/2·4.941764 + 1/2·4.955956 − 1/9.2503) × e²/4πε₀). λ_total = 1.302896 eV. k_self_exchange (ΔG=0) = 2.5515e5 s⁻¹.
- **Rates**: classical nonadiabatic Marcus with the nonequilibrium outer-sphere λ (ruling 3); k(ΔG) = (2π/ħ)|V|²(4πλkT)^−½ exp(−(ΔG+λ)²/4λkT), V = 2.7564 meV, T = 290.686 K. Peak: grid 40272 at axis = −1.305783 eV, k = 1.1325e11 s⁻¹ — the peak sits at −λ_total (−1.302896), confirming the ΔG° reading (ruling 1); `rate_peak_inside_grid: true`, so no alternative-reading keys are emitted. **Inverted region detected**: all points with axis < −1.305783 lie below the peak; first_inverted_grid_id = 5266 at axis = −1.5138 eV (most-exergonic point, per ruling 5). rate_curve.csv preserves all 61 supplied rows in original order.
- **Structure**: alignment RMSD forward = 0.0710997 Å, backward = 0.0710997 Å (matches the inspection estimate 0.07110 exactly). Dominant retained modes: forward 12 (A-frame, 680.7 cm⁻¹ band), backward 7 (B-frame, 978.6 cm⁻¹ band). Retained-mode ranges logged in diagnostics for cross-checking: frame A 0.1281–2.7753 eV/Å²/amu (186.6–868.7 cm⁻¹), frame B 0.6144–17.2132 (408.7–2163.5 cm⁻¹) — both match the inspection report.

- frame_b_hessian.npy: shape (21,21), float64, symmetric (2.8e-14). 6 ~0, 15 positive spanning 11.07083 .. 460.57373 eV/A^2.
- Rank structure matches system_manifest (null_rank=6, resolved_rank=15).

=== (2) Metadata files ===
- site_table.csv: 7 rows, columns site_id,mass_amu,label_code. Site 2 = 55.845 amu ("node_00", iron-like); sites 0,1,3,4,5,6 = 15.999 amu ("node_01..06").

I verified numerically that 521.4709 x sqrt(mass-weighted eigenvalue in eV/A^2/amu) gives plausible cm^-1 (frame A: 187-869 cm^-1; frame B: 409-2164 cm^-1) => freq_scale_factor converts sqrt(eV A^-2 amu^-1) to cm^-1, confirming the M^(-1/2) H M^(-1/2) mass-weighting convention with masses in amu.
- medium_response.json keys: shell_0_A=4.941763739779359, shell_1_A=4.957955985012061 (radii, A), span_A=9.2503 (donor-acceptor separation, A), eps_fast=1.800712950294412 (fast/optical dielectric), eps_slow=79.49976315455936 (static dielectric), coupling_eV=0.002756425977830843 (electronic coupling V), temp_K=290.6858021937607.
- driving_force_grid.csv: 63 rows, columns grid_id,axis_eV. grid_ids are unique random-looking integers (3944..97383); axis_eV in file order is strongly NON-monotonic (scrambled), values spanning -1.5138 .. +0.2692 eV. Row order must be preserved verbatim in rate_curve.csv.

=== Consistency checks already run (read-only) ===
- After reordering to site_id, A and B pairwise-distance matrices agree to <=0.147 A (same molecule, slightly deformed) => Kabsch is appropriate.
- Unweighted Kabsch (SVD with reflection correction): forward RMSD (B onto A) = backward RMSD (A onto B) = 0.07110 A; forward aligned per-site displacement magnitudes 0.032-0.100 A, total |displacement| = 0.188 A. Internal distortion is small, so lambda_inner should land near the grid range (peak of the Marcus curve at deltaG = -lambda_total is plausibly reachable by the supplied axis).
- Hessian layout: site-major block interpretation of the row permutation gives a Hessian null space overlapping the frame's rigid-body (translation+rotation) vectors with singular values 0.965-1.011, confirming site-major ordering and that rows follow frame_site_order.

=== Proposed approach (3) ===
1. Interpretation: read frame_site_order, build site-major permutations for coords (7 rows) and Hessians (21 components = repeat each site 3x); reorder everything to ascending site_id.
2. Alignment: unweighted Kabsch via SVD (P^T Q, sign-corrected for reflections), no mass weighting in the fit; RMSD reported in A. Forward: rotate/translate B into A's frame; displacement delta_q_fwd = q_B_aligned - q_A (source minus reference target). Backward: fit A onto B; delta_q_bwd = q_A_aligned - q_B.
3. Mass weighting: delta_q_mw = sqrt(m) (repeated over x,y,z) * delta_q. Mass-weighted Hessian L = M^(-1/2) H M^(-1/2) (units eV A^-2 amu^-1). Eigendecomposition; discard the 6 near-zero modes (|eig| < 1e-6), retain 15 ascending by eigenvalue; deterministic sign fix (largest-|component| entry positive). vibrational_basis_mw[f] = 15 orthonormal mass-weighted eigenvectors (21x15), site-ordered.
4. Overlaps: to compare bases across frames, rotate the transported frame's vectors with the Kabsch rotation R (block 3x3 application on the 21-vector). mode_overlap[0] = |C_A^T (R_{B->A} C_B)| (15x15, magnitude-based); mode_overlap[1] = |C_B^T (R_{A->B} C_A)|.
5. Projections: projected_displacement_mw[d] = C_ref,d (C_ref,d^T delta_q_mw,d) with reference frame A for forward, B for backward; rigid_norm = ||delta_q_mw - projection|| (component in the 6-dim external/null space), projected_norm = ||projection||.
6. transported_mode_projection (2,15,2): for each direction and each source mode k: [L2 norm of its overlap vector with the target frame's 15 retained modes, L2 norm with the target frame's 6 discarded null modes] - i.e., how much of each mode survives transport vs projects onto external motions.
7. Reorganization energies: lambda_4pt_forward = 1/2 delta_q_fwd^T H_A delta_q_fwd; lambda_4pt_backward = 1/2 delta_q_bwd^T H_B delta_q_bwd (the two single-surface halves of the four-point cycle). lambda_nm,d = 1/2 sum_k omega_k^2 q_k^2 with q_k = C^T delta_q_mw (identical analytically; closure_error = |lambda_4pt - lambda_nm| ~ numerical). lambda_inner_effective = mean of the two directional inner values; effective_inner_consistency = directional closure spread. lambda_outer = (e^2/4pi eps0)(1/eps_fast - 1/eps_slow)(1/(2a0)+1/(2a1)-1/R) with e^2/4pi eps0 = 14.3996 eV A -> approx 0.734 eV (preview arithmetic only). lambda_total = lambda_inner_effective + lambda_outer.
8. Rates: Marcus k(deltaG) = (2pi/hbar) V^2 / sqrt(4 pi lambda k_B T) * exp(-(deltaG+lambda)^2/(4 lambda k_B T)), hbar = 6.582119569e-16 eV s, k_B = 8.617333262e-5 eV/K, V = coupling_eV, T = temp_K, lambda = lambda_total; k_self_exchange is the deltaG=0 case in s^-1. rate_curve.csv preserves the supplied row order/grid_ids.
9. mode_projection (2,15,3): per direction and mode [signed modal coordinate q_k (sqrt(amu) A), lambda contribution 1/2 omega_k^2 q_k^2 (eV), fractional share of lambda_nm]. dominant_mode = argmax of the lambda contribution (zero-based).
10. Diagnostics + overview.png (mode spectra/frequencies, overlap heatmap, lambda decomposition bar chart, rate curve with peak and inverted region marked).

=== Flags / underdetermined points (4) ===
- Hessians are synthetic but fully self-consistent (PSD, exact rank 6+15, site-major, rigid-body-like null space ~0.97-1.01); no hard inconsistency found.
- Underdetermined conventions I had to choose and will document in diagnostics/analysis.py: (a) forward lambda evaluated on H_A vs H_B; (b) exact definition of lambda_inner_effective and effective_inner_consistency; (c) meaning of the 3 columns of mode_projection and 2 columns of transported_mode_projection (shapes are fixed but semantics are not given); (d) definition of first_inverted_grid_id (first file-order row with axis < -lambda_total vs first row where k falls below peak); (e) unweighted vs mass-weighted Kabsch (I choose unweighted; both give the same RMSD here since forward/backward fit is symmetric); (f) whether vibrational_basis_mw stores each frame's basis in its own native axes (my choice) or both rotated into a common frame.
- No exact eigenvector degeneracies exist (all 15 eigenvalues distinct in both frames), but eigenvectors of closely spaced modes could rotate slightly under numerical noise; deterministic sorting/sign conventions mitigate this.
- eps_fast is used as the optical dielectric in lambda_outer; span_A as the donor-acceptor distance. If a different outer-sphere convention was intended, lambda_outer (and hence lambda_total, rates, peak position, inverted-region flag) shifts.
assumptions: Row/column order of each frame's Hessian is site-major (site i occupies components 3i..3i+2) and follows frame_site_order.csv; verified indirectly via rigid-body null-space overlap (singular values 0.97-1.01) - a scrambled layout would fail this test.

Mass-weighting convention: H_mw = M^(-1/2) H M^(-1/2) with masses in amu and coordinates in Angstrom; independently verified because manifest.freq_scale_factor (521.4709) exactly converts sqrt(mass-weighted eigenvalue) to cm^-1, yielding plausible spectra (frame A 187-869 cm-1, frame B 409-2164 cm-1). An unweighted reading would give nonsensical frequencies.

Forward lambda evaluates the aligned B->A displacement with frame A's quadratic form and backward with frame B's (i.e., each direction is the single-surface half of the four-point cycle on the reference frame).

Alignment is unweighted Kabsch (mass weighting enters only the displacement vector and vibrational basis); observed forward/backward RMSD are identical (0.0710996... A) so the choice is not pivotal here, but it is a convention choice.
